name: Caruthersville Bridge
facts: The Caruthersville Bridge, first proposed in the early 1940s, had a joint state committee form in 1949; the site was chosen 1952, approved 1953, construction began 1969, and it opened December 1, 1976, with Governors Kit Bond and Ray Blanton.
The Caruthersville Bridge is a single-tower cantilever design that makes it the northernmost crossing on the Lower Mississippi River and the sole direct link between Missouri and Tennessee.

Built for US$25.8 million—about $146 million in 2025 dollars—the Caruthersville Bridge remains the only Mississippi River crossing between Cairo, Illinois, and Memphis, Tennessee, aside from the Dorena–Hickman Ferry.
